title: Enterprise SKU mapping and credit-tagging triage framework for commitments & invoices
creator: Marcus Chen
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers are submitting a growing set of non-bug billing requests that require SKU-level mapping, manual credit tagging, and special invoice exceptions. Current intake is ad hoc: sales, finance, and marketplace requests arrive via email/Sheets/Support and are inconsistently prioritized, causing delayed invoices, over-allocated credits, and manual work for Finance and Customer Success.

Goal: Create a deterministic triage framework and intake checklist that routes incoming pricing/packaging/billing requests (commitments, invoicing exceptions, marketplace crediting) into the right lanes, automates routine SKU mappings, and surfaces high-risk cases for an expedited review. The framework should reduce manual handoffs by 40% and cut time-to-resolution for prioritised enterprise billing requests by 50% within Q2.

Scope: SKU mapping rules, manual credit-tagging checklist, routing lanes (auto-resolve, finance-review, legal-review, executive-review), SLAs per lane, required artifacts, and a lightweight decision matrix for prioritization. Excluded: changes to core pricing model or product catalog ingestion pipelines (handled by Catalog team).

Approach: 1) Define canonical SKU taxonomy and mapping heuristics (pattern rules + heuristics table) that can be applied by Customer Success and automated via a small script/Playbook. 2) Create a standardized intake form and Slack-bot that collects required artifacts (deal ID, contract terms, invoice sample, marketplace transaction IDs). 3) Build routing rules that tag issues and assign to Finance, Legal, or Escalations depending on risk signals (amount > $X, sales credit required, marketplace partner involved). 4) Add acceptance criteria, handoff checklist, and a two-week pilot with top 6 enterprise customers.

Trade-offs and considerations: - Automation first but conservative: start with suggestions (human-in-the-loop) before full automation. - Avoid reworking product catalog ingestion for this effort to keep scope manageable. - Privacy and auditability: keep all changes logged and attach original signed contracts when available.

Stakeholders: Finance (Tyler Morales), Legal (Lena Ortiz), Sales Ops (Ivy Park), Customer Success (Ravi Singh), Engineering (ENG-ops leads), Marketplace Partnerships.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form deployed and integrated with Support/Slack; all required fields validated
SKU mapping heuristics documented and tested against 150 historical requests with >=85% suggestion accuracy
Routing rules implemented as triage checklist and pilot executed for 6 customers with measured SLA improvements
Handoff checklist reduces Finance manual steps by at least 40% in pilot
All triaged items generate an audit log entry and include required attachments for invoicing and legal review
decisions: Start with heuristic-based suggestions (human approval) before automating changes to invoices
Keep product catalog ingestion changes out of initial scope; rely on mapping overlay maintained by Finance
Prioritize enterprise requests flagged by revenue impact and contract complexity over smaller marketplace exceptions
